title: Security settings
purpose: See the laboratory's security and privacy contacts, set the session limits, and see what protects sign-in, sessions and patient information in this deployment, with who sets each part.
summary: Your security and privacy contacts, the session limits you set, and what protects sign-in, sessions and patient information here, with who sets each part. Only the admin role can open this page.

tasks.title: Record or change a contact
steps: Under Security and privacy contacts select [[Security contact]] or [[Privacy contact]].
Enter the name or office and any title, email and phone, explain why in [[Reason]] and select [[Save changes]].

tasks.title: Change when sessions are signed out
steps: Under Session limits select [[Staff]] or [[Client portal]].
Set [[Sign out after no activity for]] (5 to 60 minutes) and [[Longest session]] (1 to 24 hours), explain why in [[Reason]] and select [[Save changes]].

tasks.title: Find out who sets a protection
steps: Find the setting in its group (Sign-in, Sessions, Patient information or Connection) and read [[Set by]].
A deployment setting names its environment variable. Ask whoever runs the deployment to change it.

tasks.title: See who has turned on a second sign-in factor
steps: Under Sign-in read the details of Second sign-in factor. It counts active staff and client portal accounts that have a second factor (recovery codes alone do not count).

good_to_know: You change the contacts and the session limits here, each in its own form with a reason. Every other value is changed where Set by says.
A shorter limit applies from each session's next request: a session already idle longer is signed out then.
Values are read from the running application each time the page opens, so they follow the deployment as it stands.
The page states what is in force. It does not rate the deployment or say whether it meets any rule or standard.
Staff see the contacts on the laboratory profile. Client portal accounts do not see them.

sections.title: Access
paragraphs: Only the admin laboratory role can open this page, and the Setup menu lists it only for that role. Other staff roles, client portal accounts and a superuser without a laboratory role are refused. Every staff role reads the contacts on the laboratory profile instead.

sections.title: Security and privacy contacts
paragraphs: The person or office your laboratory names for questions about the security of its systems and the person or office it names for the privacy of patient information, as the laboratory records them. The application checks nothing against them and sends them nothing.

items.label: Contact
items.description: Security contact or Privacy contact. The name opens the contact's form; after saving or cancelling you return to this page. It is plain text when the laboratory is not set up yet.

items.label: Name or office
items.description: The person or office. Not recorded when the contact has never been saved or was cleared.

items.label: Title or role, Email, Phone
items.description: As recorded, or a dash when blank. The email address opens your mail program.

sections.title: Session limits
paragraphs: After how long without activity a session is signed out, and how long a session may last at most, for staff accounts and for client portal accounts. Limits never saved show the starting values, 30 minutes and 12 hours. The server checks both on every request; a page warns 2 minutes before signing out for no activity, with Stay signed in, and 5 minutes before the longest session ends.

Opening a page, saving, searching or Stay signed in counts as activity. Reading or typing on a page does not, so typing that is not saved before the sign-out is lost. Signing in again returns to the page. The admin console does not warn before signing out.

items.label: Accounts
items.description: Staff or Client portal. The name opens that audience's form; after saving or cancelling you return to this page. A portal account follows the Client portal limits and every other account the Staff limits, as the account is when each request arrives.

items.label: Sign out after no activity for
Longest session
items.description: Hours, from 1 to 24, counted from sign-in whatever the activity. Nothing extends it.

sections.title: Groups of settings
paragraphs: Sign-in: how accounts are created, the password rule, the second sign-in factor with the number of active staff and client portal accounts that have one, what changing the second factor asks for, the limit on failed sign-ins, sign-in with an emailed code and where sign-ins are recorded.

Sessions: sign-out after a period without activity and the longest session (both from Session limits above), what closing the browser does, what deactivating an account and setting a new password do to its sessions, that the browser keeps no copy of the pages, and how the session cookie is sent.

Patient information: how many active staff accounts can view patient information, how many active ticket form fields are marked as holding patient information, how person-level links and the client portal show it, and where it is kept out of.
Connection: whether HTTPS is required and which content security policy is in force.

items.label: In force
items.description: The value the running application uses now, worked out when the page opens. Counts are of active accounts or active fields at that moment.

items.label: Set by
items.description: Where the value is changed. Session limits, above: you change it on this page. This release: behaviour written into the application, changed only by a new release. Application configuration: a value in the application's configuration: config/settings.py and config/logging.py in this release, or another settings module a deployment loads instead. Deployment setting: whoever runs the deployment changes it; the environment variable is named under it. Each person: every person decides for their own account. Accounts & roles: a superuser grants it in the administration. Ticket forms: the admin role marks fields on the ticket form setup pages. Not available yet: the application has no such setting.

items.label: Details
items.description: What the value means in practice, or a dash. Debug mode notes appear when the deployment runs in debug mode, which in this release's configuration turns off the HTTPS redirect and HTTPS-only session cookies. Changed in the application configuration means that what the value depends on differs from this release's, or could not be read: a setting, config/settings.py, config/logging.py or the settings module; the details name it, and the page describes the value no further.

items.label: History
items.description: The newest 20 changes to the security contact, the privacy contact and the session limits, shown oldest first: Lab contact changed, with the contact it changed and the name before and after, or Lab session limits changed, with the accounts they apply to and each value before and after; then the reason given, the time and the administrator who made it. The laboratory profile's history lists the contact changes too.
